learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 111 km and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Equator showed longitude 111.2 km, latitude 111 km and ten-degree box 1112 km. At 60 N these were 55.6, 111 and 556. At 80 N they were 19.3, 111 and 193. Restored equator before reveal.
observations.reveal: Corrected to 56 km, used the retained Seen line for both visited latitudes, and explained converging longitude lines versus fixed latitude distance on this sphere.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshot inspected. Globe grid and yellow box were visible above readable metric chips; explanation and Seen history remained in view. Current globe was at equator while reveal referred explicitly to prior observations.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner stated history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other review judgments inspected.

prediction.reason: A concrete distance choice tests equal-degree intuition.

interaction.reason: Three latitude presets give reversible geometric and numerical contrasts.

payoff.reason: Reveal connects recorded observations with converging meridians.
payoff.evidence: Seen line supplies 60 N and 80 N values.

clarity.reason: Separate longitude and latitude metrics clarify what changes.
clarity.evidence: Latitude stayed 111 km throughout; spherical approximation stated.

transfer.reason: The general distinction is explained without a fresh application.
transfer.evidence: One degree east west is not a fixed distance.

accessibility.reason: Mode coverage was insufficient for a score.
accessibility.evidence: Named controls and text available; screen reader, keyboard sequence, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: The familiar angular unit halves in width.

visualExplanation.reason: Grid and shrinking box support the explanation.

practicalValue.evidence: Distinguishes east west from north south degree distance.

depth.reason: One geometric mechanism is explored clearly.

complexity.reason: One spatial distinction with simple comparisons.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Distinguish angular separation from ground distance and longitude from latitude.
complexity.interfaceBurden: One slider and three preset buttons.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Longitude and latitude meanings need the globe grid.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Degree symbols, kilometres and globe projection.

whyCool: A constant angular box visibly loses width as meridians converge.
caveat: Spherical approximation is explicit; no coordinate-distance application was attempted.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
